inputs.text: [excited] skeh… LY… doh… SOR… us. In Greek, "saurus" is lizard. [curious] And "scelido" was supposed to mean "strong legs," [amazed] because it had really powerful thighs.

[happily] Yes. But here's the thing: [amazed] the scientist who named it got the Greek word wrong — the one he actually wrote means "rib of beef." [playful] Without meaning to, he named it the beef-rib lizard.
[curious] And where did the beef-rib lizard live?
[serious] In England, by the sea, a hundred ninety-three million years ago. [curious] And already, [pauses] small two-legged hunters were prowling the area.
